title: Chicago pianists: Tony Jackson, Doc Cook, Clarence Jones
summary: Amacker names the outstanding Chicago pianists and praises Tony Jackson and Charlie Cook, with Miney Jones and Clarence Jones at the Owl.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Who were some outstanding piano players around Chicago?

Well, Mr. Seedman, Tony Jackson was a master there, same as he was here when they had to ride his in Chicago. For one. There was Dave Payton was another crackerjack piano player. And another, well he played at the Owl, what is his name again? He played at the Owl, that's a long second, he'll get his name in a few minutes. He was a crackerjack piano player.
Well let me ask you about somebody. Did you ever know Charlie Cook? Doc Cook?

Yeah, oh God yeah. Cook, that's the greatest musician. He's one of the greatest who was in the world. Cook was. Yeah, Cook he was, oh God. He was a top guy. He was a top guy. Cook could direct you know, and play as he direct you know. Cook was a crackerjack musician, Cook was. He was one of the best. Cook was. That was Cook, Charlie Cook, yeah he was the best. He was the greatest. There was Tony Jackson, there was Cook, and there was Dave Payton, and there's a guy that played at the Owl Theatre, and what was his name again? Jones was it? What Jones was the hell was Jones' name? Not Miney. No, not Miney Jones. I know Miney Jones, he's from down here. He went there and he's a pretty good player too, but he's pretty good around there Miney Jones. He'll make those fellas I'm talking about. Miney was a tall, slender, stiff, big fella he was there. You might have heard, because you didn't know him, you're too young to know Miney, but he walked with his leg. He dragged his left leg when he walked, stiff leg, tall fella. Miney. He wrote several pieces. I know what became of Miney, yeah. He passed. Did he pass too? Did he? He passed, did he? He's been there a good while. He died up there. What about Clarence Johnson? Did you ever hear him? Clarence Jones, that's what I'm trying to call him now. Clarence Jones, yeah. That's what I'm trying to call him now. That's what I'm trying to think of now, Clarence Jones. Who did he play with? Where? He played by himself at the Owl Theatre. I knew it would come to me eventually. Clarence Jones, I'm trying to call him Clarence Jones. He played by himself at the Owl Theatre. Did he play that jazz or what? Yeah. Clarence Jones, very nice piano player. That's what I was trying to think of Clarence Jones. Clarence Jones was Dave Payton. That was Ice Can Tate. Because Ice Can Tate was a piano piece, violinist Ice Can Tate was. And there was a half a dozen or more, all the hundreds of Cracker Jack piano players around in Chicago in those days. Did they play like the New Orleans guys? Yeah, yeah. In fact we got this, they had more stuff, a lot of them had more stuff, much and more stuff than we had down here one time. Tony Jackson went there and set Chicago fire, you know, with this jazz. When he went there. Tony did. He was such a Chicago fire, he did. Tony Jackson did. He was out of the question. Was you never heard nothing of Tony in your life?
Oh plenty. Plenty, I've heard about him. Ice and Snow? Yeah. I was one of his good nombos too. You heard of Tony, huh? Oh yeah. Well a lot of guys used to talk about him.
